# read


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Many PDFs carry a text layer, which is the text you can select and copy.
A PDF made from a digital document has an exact text layer, and reading
it costs nothing. A scanned PDF has no text layer, or it has one made by
OCR (optical character recognition), which can be poor. Old books in
Indian scripts are often worse. Many were set in legacy fonts. The text
layer of such a font reads as Latin gibberish, or it splits apart
akṣaras, the letter clusters of Devanagari. A vision model reads images,
so it can read such a page from its picture. It costs time or money for
every page, and it makes mistakes of its own.

[`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
decides page by page. The `parse` argument sets the route:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>parse=</code></th>
<th>what each page gets</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>auto</code>, the default</td>
<td>a text layer that passes the checks below is kept; a scanned page is
OCRed; a page still scanned or flagged after that goes to
<code>model</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>text</code></td>
<td>the text layer only; a scanned page stays empty</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ocr</code></td>
<td>OCR on every page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>llm</code></td>
<td><code>model</code> on every page</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`model` is any model id that the
[`urai`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#urai)
package accepts, local or hosted, such as `claude/sonnet` or
`gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`. `None` means the value of
`$VISHALAKSHI_MODEL`.

There are two entry points. The function `read_doc(path)` reads one file
and returns its pages. It does not use a vault. `Vault.read_doc(src)`
reads a file, or every PDF and image under a folder, into the vault.
Each file becomes one document. The vault keeps the text, route and
flags of each page as numbered versions. A new reading of a page never
removes an earlier reading.

## Prompts

A reading prompt tells a vision model what to return. `PRESETS` holds
four reading prompts. Each asks for the page as JSON. The JSON is a list
of items in reading order. An item is a heading, a paragraph of prose, a
verse, a table, a note or a colophon, which is the line that closes a
chapter in an Indian text. Each item has its text exactly as printed and
any number printed with it. This page calls the items of a read page
blocks.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>preset</th>
<th>use</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>generic</code></td>
<td>any printed page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sanskrit</code></td>
<td>Sanskrit prints. It names the letters that old prints make easy to
misread. It tells the model to leave out translation and commentary</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tamil</code></td>
<td>Tamil prints. It names the letters that old prints make easy to
misread</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tables</code></td>
<td>tables, read as rows of cells</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Every preset also asks for a `box` per item. The `box` is the region
that the item covers, as `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`, in fractions of the page
width and height from the top left. An app can use it to crop the block
out of the page image or to highlight it.

`reading_prompt(name, title, script, hint)` fills a preset with the
title of the document, its `script` (Devanagari by default) and a
`hint`. A hint is a sentence about this book, such as how it numbers its
verses or what to skip. A `name` that is not one of the four presets is
the whole prompt.
[`reading_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#reading_prompt)
fills `{of}`, `{title}`, `{script}` and `{hint}` in it. If the prompt
has JSON braces that are not doubled, formatting fails and
[`reading_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#reading_prompt)
returns the prompt unchanged.

use `name` itself as the prompt when it is not a preset.*

``` python
assert 'Gita' in reading_prompt('sanskrit', 'Gita') and 'ष look like प' in reading_prompt('sanskrit')
assert 'Tamil' in reading_prompt('tamil')
assert all('"box": [x0, y0, x1, y1]' in reading_prompt(k) and 'leave it out' in reading_prompt(k) for k in PRESETS)
test_eq(reading_prompt('Read it: {hint}', hint='x'), 'Read it: x')
test_eq(reading_prompt('A {script} page of {title}. {{"items": []}} {hint}', 'Gita', 'Tamil'), 'A Tamil page of Gita. {"items": []} ')
test_eq(reading_prompt('Return {"items": []} only.', 'Gita'), 'Return {"items": []} only.')   # no template: as it is
```

## Pages as images

A vision model receives a picture of the page.
[`render`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#render)
draws one page of a PDF as a PNG at `dpi` (200 by default). Some hosted
models refuse large images. When the PNG is larger than `max_bytes` (3
MB),
[`render`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#render)
returns a JPEG with a long side of at most `max_px` (3,000 pixels).
[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#fit) does
the same for an image file.

Two cuts help with hard pages.
[`halves`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#halves)
splits a landscape image into a left page and a right page. A landscape
image is usually a scan of two facing pages, called a spread.
[`page_strips`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#page_strips)
cuts a tall page into overlapping horizontal strips. The model then sees
worn or small type at a larger scale.

``` python
from pdf_oxide import Pdf
_fx = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for _i, _t in enumerate(['# Attention Is All You Need\n\nThe dominant sequence transduction models are based on recurrent or convolutional networks.',
                         '# Background\n\nThe goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU.']):
    Pdf.from_markdown(_t).save(str(_fx/f'p{_i}.pdf'))
Pdf.merge([str(_fx/'p0.pdf'), str(_fx/'p1.pdf')]).save(str(_fx/'two.pdf'))
_src = _fx/'two.pdf'
_png = render(_src, 0, dpi=72)
assert _png[:4] == b'\x89PNG'
assert render(_src, 0, dpi=300, max_bytes=1000)[:2] == b'\xff\xd8'   # over the limit: a JPEG
test_eq(fit(_png), _png); assert fit(_png, 100, 1000)[:2] == b'\xff\xd8'
from PIL import Image
def _size(b): return Image.open(io.BytesIO(b)).size
_w, _h = _size(_png)
test_eq(halves(_png), [_png])                                   # a portrait page is one page
_b = io.BytesIO(); Image.new('L', (200, 100), 255).save(_b, 'PNG'); _spread = _b.getvalue()
test_eq([_size(x) for x in halves(_spread)], [(100, 100), (100, 100)])
test_eq([_size(x) for x in page_strips(_png, 3)], [(_w, int(_h/3 + .06*_h)), (_w, int(2*_h/3 + .06*_h) - int(_h/3 - .06*_h)), (_w, _h - int(2*_h/3 - .06*_h))])
```

## Checks

[`flags`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#flags)
lists what looks wrong with a page’s text. It is how `parse='auto'`
decides that a text layer cannot be trusted.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>flag</th>
<th>meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>thin</code></td>
<td>fewer than <code>min_chars</code> (20) letters, as on a scanned
page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>replacement</code></td>
<td>the Unicode replacement character, which marks text that failed to
decode</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>legacy</code></td>
<td>more than 5 Latin-1 or typographic characters per 100 letters, which
is how a legacy Devanagari font’s text layer reads</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>split</code></td>
<td>a line that starts with a vowel sign or virāma, a piece of an akṣara
cut off from the rest</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>akshara</code></td>
<td>an akṣara that cannot be written, such as a virāma followed by a
vowel sign</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>foreign</code></td>
<td>Greek or Cyrillic letters next to Devanagari</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`disagree(a, b)` measures how far two readings of the same text differ:
the letter edits between them divided by the letters in the longer one.
Spaces, digits, daṇḍas and punctuation are ignored and vowel signs
count. A value of 0.1 or more is worth a look.

``` python
test_eq(flags('Hello world this is enough letters'), [])
test_eq(flags('क्ा and more letters here to pass'), ['akshara'])
assert 'split' in flags('कृष्ण\nा is a sign broken off here, long enough')
assert 'legacy' in flags('Jke ‘kfDr ¼ji¼ Hkxoku ¾ ™ more text here')
test_eq(flags(''), ['thin'])
assert disagree('रामः', 'रामा') > 0 and disagree('राम ॥१॥', 'राम') == 0
test_eq(disagree('', ''), None)
```

## Reading a page

[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
sends one page image to a vision model. It returns `blocks`, their text
joined as markdown (`text`), the `model` and the `cost` that the backend
reported.

With no `chat=`, the call goes through
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat).
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
records each reading once and replays it later. A repeated read of the
same page costs nothing. The recordings are in `chatcache` in the
working directory, or in the folder that `$VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE`
names. A page with no recording reaches the model only when
`$VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT` is set. Otherwise
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
raises an error that says so. `fresh=True` drops the recorded reply and
asks the model again. A reply that is not JSON raises an error and is
not recorded, and the next try reaches the model. `chat=` takes any
callable in place of a model. The tests use it to run without a model.
[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#fit) limits
the size of every image before it is sent.

A block keeps its `box` only when the box is four numbers that make a
real rectangle.
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
clamps the box to the page. It drops any other box.
[`crop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#crop) cuts
a block out of the page image by its box.

Before it sends an image,
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page)
asks
[`send_rule`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#send_rule)
whether the page may go. The level of the page is the level of its
document. It rises to Personal when `text` holds an identifier. `text`
is the text layer or the OCR text of the page. A page image cannot be
masked. A Personal page goes to a hosted model only with `allow=True` or
`pii='off'`. A Local only page never goes to a hosted model. A page that
may not be sent comes back empty, and `blocked` says why.

<a

``` python
class Fake:
    "A vision model stand-in: it answers every page with the same two items, in a code fence."
    model, calls = 'fake/vision', 0
    def __call__(self, msg):
        Fake.calls += 1
        return dict(content='```json\n{"items":[{"kind":"heading","text":"Attention Is All You Need"},{"kind":"prose","text":"The dominant sequence transduction models are based on recurrent networks."}]}\n```', usage=dict(cost=0.01))
_r = read_page(_png, chat=Fake())
test_eq([b['kind'] for b in _r.blocks], ['heading', 'prose'])
assert _r.text.startswith('## Attention') and _r.cost == .01
class Boxed(Fake):
    "A reader that gives boxes: one sane, one out of range, one reversed, one not a box."
    def __call__(self, msg):
        return dict(content=json.dumps(dict(items=[dict(kind='heading', text='Attention', box=[.1, .05, .9, .1]), dict(kind='prose', text='The dominant models', box=[-.1, .2, 1.2, .5]),
                                                   dict(kind='prose', text='are recurrent', box=[.9, .6, .1, .7]), dict(kind='note', text='x', box='top')])))
_r = read_page(_png, chat=Boxed())
test_eq([b.get('box') for b in _r.blocks], [[.1, .05, .9, .1], [0., .2, 1., .5], None, None])
from PIL import Image
_w, _h = Image.open(io.BytesIO(_png)).size
_c = crop(_png, [0, 0, .5, .5], pad=0)
test_eq((_c[:4], Image.open(io.BytesIO(_c)).size), (b'\x89PNG', (round(_w / 2), round(_h / 2))))
_cw, _ch = Image.open(io.BytesIO(crop(_png, [.4, .4, .6, .6]))).size
assert abs(_cw - .24 * _w) <= 1 and abs(_ch - .24 * _h) <= 1
test_eq(crop(_png, None), _png); test_eq(crop(_png, [.5, .5, .5, .6]), _png)
test_eq(_md([dict(kind='table', rows=[['a', 'b'], ['1', '2']])]), '| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |')
```

``` python
backends()
```

## Reading a document

`read_doc(path)` takes a PDF or a page image and returns one row per
page: `{page, text, route, flags}`. A page that the model read also has
`blocks`, `model` and `cost`. `route` says where the text came from. Its
values are `text` (the text layer), `ocr`, `model`, and `scanned` when
nothing read the page. `pages=[...]` limits which pages may go to the
model. The other pages keep their text layer. `workers` (4 by default)
sets how many pages are read at the same time.

Privacy works page by page, as in
[`read_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_page).
When any page is going to a model and `pii` is not `off`,
[`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
first checks the whole text layer for a sensitive doctype. A document
whose text clearly reads as a passport or a payslip is Local only before
any page image leaves. `local_model=` or a built `local_chat=` reads the
pages that the hosted `model` may not read. Without either, those pages
keep their text layer and carry `blocked`. A scanned page has no text to
check. Only the level of its document applies to it.

These options control a long read:

- `progress(done, total, page, route, cost)` is called once with
  `done=0`, then after each page that was due for the model. If it
  returns False, the reading stops. The pages not yet read keep their
  text layer or OCR. The result’s `cancelled` is True, and `unread`
  lists those pages.
  [`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
  ignores an error raised inside `progress`.
- `cache=` keeps each model reading as a JSON file,
  `{page, items, cost, model}`. The file is in a folder (`p0001.json`,
  or `p0001a.json` and `p0001b.json` for the two halves of a spread), or
  at the path that a function `cache(page, half)` returns. A cached page
  is not sent again. Its `cost` is None, because nothing was spent, and
  `cached` is True.
- `redo=[...]` reads those pages again even when they are cached. After
  the new reading is saved, the old reading moves to a sibling folder.
  The folder has the name of the cache folder with `_prev` added. A
  number is added to the file name when an older copy is already there.
- `spread=True` treats a landscape page as two facing pages and reads
  the halves in turn. `strips=k` sends each image as `k` overlapping
  strips.
- `clean=` is a function that
  [`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
  applies to the text of each block before it keeps the block.
- `tries=n` tries a failing page up to `n` times. It waits `RETRY_WAIT`
  seconds (10) after the first failure, 20 after the second, and so on.
  A page that still fails keeps its text layer, carries its `error`, and
  is listed in the result’s `failed`. Without `tries`,
  [`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc)
  raises the first error.

`doc_cost(rows)` adds up the cost of the pages that a model read.
`doc_files(folder)` lists the PDFs and images under a folder.

### read_doc

``` python
def read_doc(
    path, parse:str='auto', model:str=None, preset:str='generic', title:str='', script:str='', hint:str='',
    pages:NoneType=None, dpi:int=200, out:NoneType=None, workers:int=4, chat:NoneType=None,
    pii:str='redact', # what `read_page` applies to each page; `off` sends Personal pages too, never Local only ones
    level:str=None, # the document's level; None -> open, raised to Local only when its text reads as a sensitive type
    allow:bool=False, # allow once, for Personal pages
    local_model:str=None, # reads the pages a hosted `model` may not; None -> those pages keep their text layer
    local_chat:NoneType=None, # a built local reader instead of `local_model`
    progress:NoneType=None, # `progress(done, total, page, route, cost)`; False stops the reading
    spread:bool=False, # a landscape page is a two-page spread: its halves read in turn (`halves`)
    strips:int=1, # each image sent as overlapping strips (`read_page`)
    cache:NoneType=None, # a folder, or `cache(page, half)` -> a path: each reading kept as JSON there and not sent again
    redo:NoneType=None, # pages read again though cached; the old reading moved to `<folder>_prev/` once the new one is in
    clean:NoneType=None, # `clean(text)` -> text, made of every block's text before it is kept
    tries:int=None, # a page that fails this many times is left out and listed in `failed`; None raises its error
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Read each page of a PDF or page image, keeping a sound text layer and
sending scanned or flagged pages to `model`, and return one row per
page.*

``` python
test_eq((len(Halves.msg), 'overlapping strips' in Halves.msg[-1]), (4, True))
class Flaky(Fake):
    "Fails its first call, as a model starting slowly does."
    n = 0
    def __call__(self, msg):
        Flaky.n += 1
        if Flaky.n == 1: raise TimeoutError('slow start')
        return super().__call__(msg)
class Down(Fake):
    def __call__(self, msg): raise TimeoutError('down')
RETRY_WAIT = 0

_m = read_doc(_src, parse='llm', chat=Down(), out=_d/'.out', workers=1, tries=2, pages=[0], cache=(_fd := Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())))

test_fail(lambda: read_doc(_src, parse='llm', chat=Down(), out=_d/'.out', workers=1), contains='down')
RETRY_WAIT = 10
```

## Into the vault

`Vault.read_doc(src)` reads a file, or every PDF and image under a
folder. It adds each file to the vault as one document. Search and `ask`
reach the document like any other. It also keeps each page as a version
in the `read_pages` table. A page gets a new version only when its text,
route or blocks changed. Reading a file twice with the same result adds
nothing.

Each new version is scanned for personal information, and the findings
are filed against it (see [pii](09_pii.ipynb)). A new document starts at
the shelf’s floor. A document already in the vault keeps its own level.

`Vault.pages(doc_id)` returns the latest version of each current page.
`history=True` returns every version of those pages. A shorter file
marks pages beyond its end stale. Their readings remain in `read_pages`.
They are not indexed or returned by default. The vault writes every page
that a hosted model read to the send log.

Use `stale=True` on `pages`, `search`, `sections`, `context`,
`document`, `doc_context`, `ask` or `federate` to include retained stale
pages. Retrieval builds a temporary in-memory index for this request. It
never adds stale text to the stored index. Hybrid search can still
return unrelated current pages for a missing word.

`prune_stale(doc_id=None, dry_run=False)` deletes every reading of stale
pages on this shelf. It returns each document id, page number and
version count. `dry_run=True` returns the same report without deleting
anything. The method is Python-only, like `housekeep`.

The result of
[`Vault.read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#vault.read_doc)
is the ingest result with these keys added: `routes` (how many pages
took each route), `flagged`, `blocked`, `cost`, `model_pages`,
`cancelled`, `unread` and `failed`.

`Vault.reparse(doc_id, pages=[...])` reads pages of a document again. By
default it uses the model (`parse='llm'`) and the preset, script and
hint of the document. It files the new readings as new versions and
re-indexes the document. Use it when a page came out badly and a better
model should read it. `reparse` returns the ingest result with these
keys added: `pages` (the pages it read), `changed` (the pages whose text
changed), `blocked`, `cost`, `model_pages`, `cancelled` and `unread`.

Both methods take `progress`. A cancelled or failed read of a document
already in the vault leaves its unread and failed pages as they were.
When a folder is read with `cache=`, each file caches in its own
subfolder. The subfolder has the file’s path below the folder, extension
included, so `a/report.pdf` and `b/report.pdf` do not share one. A cache
written by an earlier version, which named each file by its stem alone,
is not reused. Those pages are read again.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vishalakshi/blob/main/vishalakshi/read.py#L426"

A three-page PDF shortened to two pages keeps its last page as stale.
Both read paths exclude that page from retrieval. A dry run preserves
every reading. Pruning removes them.

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as _short_dir:
    _short_root = Path(_short_dir)
    _short_files = []
    for _page_no, _text in enumerate(['Orchard apples grow in the sunny garden.', 'Sailing boats cross the blue ocean.', 'Zebramarker belongs to the vanished last page.']):
        _page_path = _short_root/f'p{_page_no}.pdf'
        Pdf.from_markdown(_text).save(str(_page_path))
        _short_files.append(str(_page_path))
    _short_src = _short_root/'book.pdf'
    _short_vault = Vault(_short_root/'vault.db', offline=True)
    for _read_again in ('read_doc', 'reparse'):
        Pdf.merge(_short_files).save(str(_short_src))
        _short_id = _short_vault.read_doc(_short_src, parse='text')['doc_id']
        Pdf.merge(_short_files[:2]).save(str(_short_src))
        if _read_again == 'read_doc': _short_vault.read_doc(_short_src, parse='text')
        else: _short_vault.reparse(_short_id, parse='text')
        test_eq(_short_vault.pages(_short_id).attrgot('page'), [0, 1])
        _retained = _short_vault.pages(_short_id, stale=True)
        test_eq(_retained.attrgot('page'), [0, 1, 2])
        assert _retained[2].stale
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in _short_vault.document(_short_id).text
        assert 'Zebramarker' in _short_vault.document(_short_id, stale=True).text
        test_eq(_short_vault.search('Zebramarker', where="content like '%Zebramarker%'"), [])
        assert any('Zebramarker' in h.snippet for h in _short_vault.search('Zebramarker', stale=True))
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in str(_short_vault.sections('Zebramarker'))
        assert 'Zebramarker' in str(_short_vault.sections('Zebramarker', stale=True))
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in str(_short_vault.context('Zebramarker', code=0, shelves=0).results)
        assert 'Zebramarker' in str(_short_vault.context('Zebramarker', code=0, shelves=0, stale=True).results)
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in _short_vault.doc_context(_short_id, 'what remains?', related=0).doc.text
        assert 'Zebramarker' in _short_vault.doc_context(_short_id, 'what remains?', related=0, stale=True).doc.text
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in str(_short_vault.federate('Zebramarker', repo=False, env=False, grep=False, shelves=None).hits)
        assert 'Zebramarker' in str(_short_vault.federate('Zebramarker', repo=False, env=False, grep=False, shelves=None, stale=True).hits)
        assert 'Zebramarker' not in _short_vault.document(_short_id).text
        test_eq(_short_vault.search('Zebramarker', where="content like '%Zebramarker%'"), [])
        _preview = _short_vault.prune_stale(_short_id, dry_run=True)
        test_eq([r['page'] for r in _preview], [2])
        test_eq(len(_short_vault.pages(_short_id, stale=True)), 3)
        test_eq(_short_vault.prune_stale(), _preview)
        test_eq(_short_vault.pages(_short_id, history=True, stale=True).attrgot('page'), [0, 1])
    _paper_vault = _short_vault.shelf('papers')
    Pdf.merge(_short_files).save(str(_short_src))
    _paper_id = _paper_vault.read_doc(_short_src, parse='text')['doc_id']
    Pdf.merge(_short_files[:2]).save(str(_short_src))
    _paper_vault.reparse(_paper_id, parse='text', pages=[0])
    _paper_vault.mark_stale(_paper_id, reason='changed source')
    _paper_age = _paper_vault.doc(_paper_id)['added_at']
    _sidecars = {p: p.read_bytes() for p in _short_root.glob('*.usearch*')}
    assert 'Zebramarker' in _paper_vault.document(_paper_id, stale=True).text
    assert any(h.stale for h in _paper_vault.search('Zebramarker', stale=True))
    test_eq(_paper_vault.doc(_paper_id)['added_at'], _paper_age)
    assert all(p.read_bytes() == data for p, data in _sidecars.items())
    test_eq(_paper_vault.pages(_paper_id).attrgot('page'), [0, 1])
    _short_vault.db.close()
_preview
```
